cover.title: Even the guards here have seen things

lines.text: Even the guards here have seen things.
The Tower of London. A fortress on the River Thames for nearly a thousand years. A palace, a prison... and a place of execution.
In 1536, Queen Anne Boleyn was beheaded inside these walls. She's buried in the Tower's own chapel.
October 1817. The Keeper of the Crown Jewels, Edmund Swifte, sat down to supper with his family in the Jewel House.
He later wrote that a glowing tube, like bubbling blue liquid, appeared above the table... and moved toward his wife.
1864. A soldier was found collapsed at his post. Charged with sleeping on duty, he said a white figure came at him... and his bayonet went straight through it.
Other soldiers backed up his story. He was cleared.
And for centuries, people have claimed to see a woman walking near the place where Anne Boleyn died.
Would you take the night shift here? Comment night shift, partner.
